name: WISE 0855−0714
what_it_is: a Y-type brown dwarf with a temperature of about 250 K (around -20 °C), the coldest known object of its kind

motion.how_measured: position measured in each WISE image, then a straight-line fit through time

notes: 220 images were left out because a catalogue star was closer than 9" to the moving target (one SPHEREx pixel is 6.15"; such blends cannot be separated).
Below 2.4 µm: -0.009 ± 0.009 mJy (S/N -1.0) — not detected: invisible at short wavelengths.
4.4–4.9 µm: 0.624 ± 0.083 mJy (S/N 7) — detected where the coldest brown dwarfs emit most.
3.2–3.5 µm (methane band): 0.016 ± 0.029 mJy — not detected: methane absorbs this band.
The flux rises steeply from 4 to 4.6 µm, as expected for an object of only ~250 K.

what_to_look_for_in_the_movie: a faint dot that crawls to the right (west) by about 114 arcseconds between 2010 and 2024, visible at 4.6 micrometres but invisible at shorter wavelengths
